pr_title: Add workaround to GPIO MCUX driver for non contiguous pins
pr_body:
Some iMX RT parts have a non contiguous set of pins available on certain GPIO ports (for example, GPIO0_0-GPIO0_10 are defined, as well as GPIO0_20-GPIO0_31, but GPIO0_11-GPIO0_19 are absent). Add a workaround to the iMX RT gpio driver to correctly select the GPIO pinmux register in these cases.

This PR also fixes the GPIO active flags on the RT1024 and RT1170 EVK LEDs, as these were discovered to be incorrect in testing.

Fixes #44391
pr_comments: @hakehuang I'll wait on your approval before merging
DNM both while we're waiting on @hakehuang but also because this rings a bell for me and I want to double check if there is a standard way to express this in devicetree.

> I want to double check if there is a standard way to express this in devicetree.

There is; `gpio-reserved-ranges`: https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/59250f8a7f3a60a2661b84cbafc1e0eb5d05ec9b/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/gpio/gpio.txt#L150

It seems like it would be a bit cleaner to express this in the .dtsi files for each target that has this restriction. You could save the entire value of the array property in ROM and then quickly check if a given GPIO is valid at runtime or something like that.

Edit: I just want to make it clear that I'm not blocking the PR over this, just suggesting a further improvement.

@mbolivar-nordic I agree that using `gpio-reserved-ranges` would be a cleaner approach to use here, but is there a way to access the index of the reserved GPIO and the number of reserved GPIOs induvidually? Something similar to the way that an array of register properties will have both a size and reg property available in the devicetree. The other option is of course just to create an array out of the `gpio-reserved-ranges` property and index into it properly to obtain each pair of (`gpio-idx, num-rsvd`) values, but I wanted to check if there was a better method to use.
@mbolivar-nordic, can you consider @danieldegrasse response to your point and if okay remove the DNM label you added?
I didn't have time to get to this by code freeze, so I'm removing the DNM
